title: Unrivaled adds New York as a tour stop for regular-season games
content:
Unrivaled announced on Thursday that it will be returning to Brooklyn as part of its national tour in its third season. Four Unrivaled teams will play regular-season games on Jan. 22 at Barclays Center.

The professional 3×3 league played its semifinal playoff games at Barclays Center last season in front of sell-out crowds. This season’s games in New York will be simulcast on TNT, truTV and HBO Max.

The league will announce more tour stops at a later date.

Unrivaled commissioner Micky Lawler said in the press release that the decision to return to New York was a “no-brainer.”  He added: “We can’t wait to be back in Brooklyn to once again showcase the incredible talent of Unrivaled in front of our passionate, energetic Unrivaled fans in New York.”

League president Alex Bazzell said in August that the league plans to play four times as many road venues as it did last season, and Unrivaled’s road games will again include road playoff games.

Unrivaled spent its 2025 inaugural season in Medley, Fla., its home base outside of Miami, and last year, it played a late January double-header in Philadelphia, setting a women’s hoops attendance record at the Xfinity Mobile Arena (21,490). The league’s March semifinals last season at Barclays Center was played in front of a sold-out crowd of more than 18,000 fans with celebrities such as Jason Sudeikis, Wanda Sykes and Issa Rae taking in the festivities.

In its third season, Unrivaled is seeking to build its brand and get in front of more fans for in-person experiences. Sephora Arena, Unrivaled’s home base in Florida, seats around 1,000. Despite the significant increase in overall ticket sales in Year 2, due to the massive in-person crowds in Philadelphia and Brooklyn, viewership numbers decreased in the league’s sophomore season.

Its title game, broadcast on TNT and TruTV, experienced a 14 percent dip compared to the 2025 title game while overall viewership was down nine percent year-over-year.
